wholeLesson.title: Diagnostic Frameworks
wholeLesson.summary: Diagnostic frameworks organize evidence. They do not replace clinical judgment, and their criteria should not be mixed casually.
wholeLesson.application: Name the framework, show the criteria that are present, explain confounders, and document severity using that framework rather than combining thresholds from unrelated systems.

lesson.heading: Apply GLIM in two steps
lesson.body: After risk screening, GLIM diagnosis requires at least one phenotypic criterion and at least one etiologic criterion. Phenotypic criteria are weight loss, low BMI, and reduced muscle mass. Etiologic criteria are reduced intake or assimilation and inflammation or disease burden. Assess all five criteria where possible. A diagnosis can be established when at least one phenotypic and one etiologic criterion are demonstrated despite a practical barrier to other measurements; excluding malnutrition requires assessment of all five. Muscle strength may inform the wider assessment, but it is not a substitute for muscle mass in the GLIM diagnostic algorithm.

lesson.heading: Apply Academy and ASPEN characteristics
lesson.body: The Academy and ASPEN adult framework evaluates insufficient energy intake, weight loss, loss of muscle mass, loss of subcutaneous fat, fluid accumulation, and diminished functional status measured by handgrip strength. At least two characteristics support diagnosis, interpreted within the relevant acute illness, chronic illness, or social and environmental context.

lesson.heading: Do not diagnose from albumin
lesson.body: Albumin and prealbumin are influenced strongly by inflammation, capillary permeability, fluid status, organ function, and other factors. ASPEN does not recommend using them as proxy measures of total body protein or muscle mass, or as stand alone nutrition markers.

keyPoints: GLIM requires both phenotype and etiology.
Severity is not simply the number of criteria present.
Albumin can inform risk and inflammation, but it does not diagnose malnutrition.
